## Standing rules

1. One Python package, `oxide` (ADR-0011). A new package or dependency needs a reuse, packaging or API reason.
2. Legacy v1 (`ac985b28`) is evidence, not a template. Reusing it requires a stated SPEC requirement, a boundary-fit reason and tests. No legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations or cache locations; derived state is rebuildable from captured source.
3. Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`, I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`. LadybugDB objects, native IDs, rows and Cypher stay inside `oxide.storage`; the API exposes only domain values. Integrations (the CLI, `oxide mcp`, editors) are clients of `oxide.api` and never parse, route or select.
4. When SPEC and code disagree, SPEC wins. If SPEC is ambiguous, record the ambiguity and a proposal; don't invent permanent ID, schema, transport or model policy to unblock scaffolding.
5. Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Lexical entry points, TreeRouter, the heuristic value and the packer need no model or network.
6. Models judge; deterministic code decides thresholds, traversal, stopping, inclusion, budget, fallback and packing. A `DecisionProvider` seam behind `oxide.core.packing.value` carries abstention and a deterministic fallback; JEV and every learned judge stay optional, and CI never runs a live judge.
7. Structure comes before similarity: retrieval finds entry points, routing finds context, and the TreeIndex keeps cross-edges.
8. Native libraries (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX, hashing) do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy.

10. Frozen baselines keep their provenance. Never regenerate gold or erase a negative result to make a challenger pass; promoting a quality change to a default needs gate evidence.

2	
3	Routed candidates get a heuristic relevance value (the Rust ``heuristic-evidence/1``
4	rules), then one greedy pass takes the best candidate whose group (the item plus a
5	header of every enclosing declaration not yet shown) fits the remaining budget,
6	whole or reduced to its header view, otherwise omits it with a reason. Fit is
7	checked by rendering the exact payload, so ``used <= budget`` holds by construction.
8	
9	A symbol's view is its declaration. A parsed Python file's view is its module-level
10	source (imports, constants, top-level statements): the runs of non-blank lines
11	between its top-level declarations, never the whole file; its header view is the
12	first run, and it competes only when retrieval found the file. Other files, modules
13	and the repository are containers without a view.
14	
15	A ``paths`` hint names where the relevant code lives: candidates in a hinted file are
16	taken before all others (value, floor and order unchanged within each tier), and the
17	hinted file itself contributes only its header view, so its declarations, not its
18	module-level glue, get the budget.
19	
20	Units are ``oxide-units-v1``: each run of word characters costs ceil(len/4), each
21	newline 1, other whitespace 0, any other character 1. They claim no model's
22	tokenizer. Payload ``oxide-payload-v3``: per item ``### <path>:<l1>-<l2> <names>``

24	first-selection order, spans in byte order, overlapping spans of one file merged and
25	counted once.

115	    name = provider.identity
116	    try:
117	        found = provider.judge(tuple(candidates))
118	        failure = None if isinstance(found, Mapping) else "returned no mapping"
119	        if failure is None and not found.keys() <= values.keys():
120	            failure = "judged an unknown candidate"
121	    except Exception as error:  # any provider failure leaves the deterministic path
122	        failure = f"failed ({type(error).__name__})"
123	    if failure is not None:
124	        return {k: (score, f"{basis}, {name} {failure}") for k, (score, basis) in values.items()}
125	    out = {}
126	    for key, (score, basis) in values.items():
127	        got = found.get(key, ...)
128	        if got is ...:
129	            out[key] = (score, f"{basis}, {name} missing")
130	        elif got is None:
131	            out[key] = (score, f"{basis}, {name} abstained")
132	        elif isinstance(got, (int, float)) and not isinstance(got, bool) and 0 <= got <= 1:
133	            out[key] = (float(got), f"judged by {name}")  # NaN and infinities fail the range
134	        else:
135	            out[key] = (score, f"{basis}, {name} invalid")
136	    return out
137	
138	
139	def display(key: str) -> str:
140	    return key.rsplit("#", 1)[1] if key.startswith("symbol:") else key.split(":", 1)[-1]
141	
142	
143	def ancestors(key: str) -> list[str]:
144	    """Enclosing declarations of a symbol, outermost first."""
145	    if not key.startswith("symbol:"):
146	        return []
147	    file, path = key.rsplit("#", 1)
148	    segments = path.split(".")
149	    return [f"{file}#{'.'.join(segments[:i])}" for i in range(1, len(segments))]
150	
151	
152	def header_end(data: bytes, start: int, end: int, name: str) -> int | None:
153	    """End of the header view: through the first line naming the entity, at most
154	    ``MAX_HEADER_LINES`` (the first line when none does). None when not smaller."""
155	    named = re.compile(rb"(?<![\w\x80-\xff])" + re.escape(name.encode()) + rb"(?![\w\x80-\xff])")
156	    at, first = start, None
157	    for line in data[start:end].splitlines(keepends=True)[:MAX_HEADER_LINES]:
158	        at += len(line)
159	        first = first or at
160	        if named.search(line):
161	            return at if at < end else None
162	    return first if first is not None and first < end else None
163	
164	
165	def module_regions(data: bytes, declarations: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
166	    """Byte ranges of a file's module-level source: maximal runs of whole lines that
167	    no top-level declaration touches, from the first to the last non-blank line."""
168	    spans = sorted(declarations)
169	    regions: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
170	    run: tuple[int, int] | None = None
171	    at = d = 0
172	    for line in data.split(b"\n"):
173	        start, end = at, at + len(line)
174	        at = end + 1
175	        while d < len(spans) and spans[d][1] <= start:
176	            d += 1
177	        if d < len(spans) and spans[d][0] <= end:
178	            if run is not None:
179	                regions.append(run)
180	            run = None
181	        elif line.strip():
182	            run = (run[0] if run else start, end)
183	    return [*regions, run] if run is not None else regions
184	
185	
186	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
187	class _Piece:
188	    entity: Entity
189	    start: int
190	    end: int
191	    reason: str
192	
193	
194	class _Packer:
195	    def __init__(
196	        self,
197	        budget: int,
198	        source: Callable[[SourceRef], bytes],
199	        declarations: Mapping[str, list[tuple[int, int]]],
200	    ) -> None:
201	        self.budget = budget
202	        self.source = source
203	        self.declarations = declarations
204	        self.cache: dict[str, bytes] = {}
205	
206	    def data(self, ref: SourceRef) -> bytes:
207	        if ref.path not in self.cache:
208	            self.cache[ref.path] = self.source(ref)
209	        return self.cache[ref.path]
210	
211	    def render(self, pieces: list[_Piece]) -> list[ContextItem] | None:
212	        """Items for ``pieces``; None when a span is not UTF-8 text."""
213	        by_file: dict[str, list[_Piece]] = {}
214	        for piece in pieces:
215	            assert piece.entity.source is not None
216	            by_file.setdefault(piece.entity.source.path, []).append(piece)
217	        items = []
218	        for path, group in by_file.items():
219	            spans: list[list[_Piece]] = []
220	            for piece in sorted(group, key=lambda p: (p.start, p.end)):
221	                if spans and piece.start < max(p.end for p in spans[-1]):
222	                    spans[-1].append(piece)
223	                else:
224	                    spans.append([piece])
225	            for span in spans:
226	                item = self.item(path, span)
227	                if item is None:
228	                    return None
229	                items.append(item)
230	        return items
231	
232	    def item(self, path: str, span: list[_Piece]) -> ContextItem | None:
233	        start, end = min(p.start for p in span), max(p.end for p in span)
234	        ref = span[0].entity.source
235	        assert ref is not None
236	        data = self.data(ref)
237	        try:
238	            body = data[start:end].decode("utf-8")
239	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
240	            return None
241	        entities: dict[str, ItemEntity] = {}
242	        for piece in span:
243	            source = piece.entity.source
244	            assert source is not None
245	            complete = start <= source.start and source.end <= end
246	            entities.setdefault(
247	                piece.entity.key,
248	                ItemEntity(piece.entity.key, display(piece.entity.key), complete, piece.reason),
249	            )
250	        labels = ", ".join(
251	            "(module-level)"
252	            if e.key.startswith("file:")
253	            else e.name + ("" if e.complete else " (header)")
254	            for e in entities.values()
255	        )
256	        first = data.count(b"\n", 0, start) + 1
257	        last = data.count(b"\n", 0, max(start, end - 1)) + 1
258	        text = f"### {path}:{first}-{last} {labels}\n{body}"
259	        text += "" if text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
260	        source = SourceRef(path, start, end, ref.digest)
261	        return ContextItem(source, (first, last), tuple(entities.values()), units(text), text)
262	
263	    def fits(self, pieces: list[_Piece]) -> list[ContextItem] | None:
264	        items = self.render(pieces)
265	        if items is None or sum(i.units for i in items) > self.budget:
266	            return None
267	        return items
268	
269	    def view(self, entity: Entity, header: bool, reason: str) -> list[_Piece]:
270	        """The pieces of a full or header view; empty when there is no such view."""
271	        source = entity.source
272	        assert source is not None
273	        if entity.category == "file":
274	            regions = module_regions(self.data(source), self.declarations[entity.key])
275	            chosen = (regions[:1] if len(regions) > 1 else []) if header else regions
276	            return [_Piece(entity, start, end, reason) for start, end in chosen]
277	        if not header:
278	            return [_Piece(entity, source.start, source.end, reason)]
279	        end = header_end(self.data(source), source.start, source.end, entity.name)
280	        return [] if end is None else [_Piece(entity, source.start, end, reason)]
281	
282	
283	def pack(
284	    pool: list[Candidate],
285	    scopes: dict[str, Entity],
286	    budget: int,
287	    source: Callable[[SourceRef], bytes],
288	    declarations: Mapping[str, list[tuple[int, int]]],
289	    judge: DecisionProvider | None = None,
290	) -> tuple[list[ContextItem], list[Omission]]:
291	    """``pool`` in graph order (entry points first); ``scopes`` holds every enclosing
292	    declaration of a pool symbol; ``declarations`` the top-level declaration byte
293	    ranges of every parsed Python file in the pool; ``judge`` an optional provider,
294	    asked once about the candidates that have a source and are not containers.
295	    Returns packed items and every omission."""
296	    packer = _Packer(budget, source, declarations)
297	    omissions: list[Omission] = []
298	    scored = []
299	
300	    def container(c: Candidate) -> bool:
301	        category = c.entity.category
302	        return category not in ("symbol", "file") or (
303	            category == "file" and c.entity.key not in declarations
304	        )
305	
306	    asked = [c for c in pool if not container(c) and c.entity.source is not None]
307	    values = judged(judge, asked) if judge is not None and asked else {}
308	    for position, candidate in enumerate(pool):
309	        key = candidate.entity.key
310	        score, basis = values.get(key) or value(candidate)
311	        if container(candidate):
312	            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "container"))
313	        elif candidate.entity.source is None:
314	            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "no source"))
315	        elif score < INCLUDE_FLOOR:
316	            why = f"value {score:.2f} below floor" + (f", {basis}" if key in values else "")
317	            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", why))
318	        elif not packer.view(candidate.entity, False, ""):
319	            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "no module-level source"))
320	        else:
321	            basis += ", hinted path" if candidate.hinted else ""
322	            scored.append(
323	                (not candidate.hinted, -score, position, candidate, f"value {score:.2f}, {basis}")
324	            )
325	    pieces: list[_Piece] = []
326	    items: list[ContextItem] = []
327	    planned = 0
328	    for *_, candidate, reason in sorted(scored, key=lambda s: s[:3]):
329	        entity = candidate.entity
330	        if planned >= MAX_ITEMS:
331	            omissions.append(Omission(entity.key, "selection", f"item cap {MAX_ITEMS}"))
332	            continue
333	        shown = {p.entity.key for p in pieces}
334	        prerequisites: list[_Piece] = []
335	        for outer in ancestors(entity.key):
336	            if outer not in shown and outer in scopes:
337	                header = packer.view(scopes[outer], True, f"header of {display(entity.key)}")
338	                prerequisites += header or packer.view(scopes[outer], False, "prerequisite")
339	        outline = candidate.hinted and entity.category == "file"
340	        for reduced in (True,) if outline and packer.view(entity, True, "") else (False, True):
341	            view = packer.view(entity, reduced, reason + (", header view" if reduced else ""))
342	            fitted = packer.fits([*pieces, *prerequisites, *view]) if view else None
343	            if fitted is not None:
344	                pieces += [*prerequisites, *view]
345	                items = fitted
346	                planned += 1
347	                break
348	        else:
349	            smallest = packer.view(entity, True, "") or packer.view(entity, False, "")
350	            assert smallest
351	            alone = packer.render([*prerequisites, *smallest])
352	            too_large = alone is None or sum(i.units for i in alone) > budget
353	            omissions.append(
354	                Omission(entity.key, "packing", "too large" if too_large else "budget")
355	            )
356	    return items, omissions

# Frozen evaluation inputs

Read-only oracles for the quality gates. Never regenerate them to make a failure pass.
Experiments are only for claims a test can't settle (AGENTS.md § How to work); ordinary
implementation is accepted on tests plus `mise run verify`, and changes to retrieval,
routing or packing must also pass the ContextBench gates.

| Path | Read by |
|---|---|
| `structural-v1/` | `tests/python/test_baseline.py`: exact reproduction of the Rust structural baseline |
| `contextbench-py/{tasks,gold-audit}.json`, `contextbench-py/baseline-v19/` | `tests/python/contextbench.py` (`TASKS`, `AUDIT`, `BASELINE`), in `verify` |
| `contextbench-ts/{tasks,gold-audit}.json`, `contextbench-ts/baseline-v16/` | `tests/python/contextbench_ts.py`, `mise run contextbench-ts` |

Path labels inside frozen files (`docs/phase-6/...`) are their original locations,
kept byte-for-byte; the files themselves are history at `013e791`.

## ContextBench protocol

- **Tasks.** Fixture queries (`fixtures/benchmark.json`, `structural_benchmark.json`) plus
  `EuniAI/ContextBench` `data/full.parquet` tasks (sha256 `2f56535b…`) filtered by a
  file-count cost rule: 37 Python tasks (requests, flask, seaborn, xarray, pytest) and 81
  TypeScript tasks (mui, vue, vscode, code-server, darkreader). Gold is the
  human-annotated line spans; the audit marks each span verified or unverified, never
  dropped, and only verified gold is gated.
- **Splits are by repository.** Held-out is xarray and pytest (Python), mui and vue
  (TypeScript). Develop on dev; read held-out results only to evaluate a finished change.
- **Metrics** (macro means per split). Entry: `entry_recall@1/5/20`, `entry_mrr`,
  `entry_file_recall`. Routing: `routed_coverage`. Packing at 256/1,024/4,096 units:
  `span_recall`, `line_recall`, `file_recall`, `utilization`, `gold_unit_share`. Each loss
  is tagged with the stage that caused it.
- **Gate rules.** Per split, every gated metric stays at or above its frozen value minus
  0.02; bundles stay within budget, are deterministic and never fail; corpus identities
  match the manifest. Output compatibility (entry order, routed set, payload digests) is
  checked separately, and a version bump is a versioned difference, not a regression.
- **Freezing.** A failing gate is investigated, not re-frozen. An intended, reviewed
  change is frozen as a new `baseline-vN` beside the current one, with a README giving the
  reason and the diff against the previous version: run
  `uv run --locked python tests/python/contextbench.py run --out fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-vN`
  under the resource limits, switch `BASELINE`, and remove the superseded directory in the
  same change (git history keeps it).
- **Recording.** A verdict is one row in [`docs/decisions.md`](../../docs/decisions.md),
  plus a short report only if a gate, test or comment will cite it.

Commands, corpora and resource limits are in [workflow](../../docs/agents/workflow.md).

def pack(
    pool: list[Candidate],
    scopes: dict[str, Entity],
    budget: int,
    source: Callable[[SourceRef], bytes],
    declarations: Mapping[str, list[tuple[int, int]]],
    judge: DecisionProvider | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[ContextItem], list[Omission]]:
    """``pool`` in graph order (entry points first); ``scopes`` holds every enclosing
    declaration of a pool symbol; ``declarations`` the top-level declaration byte
    ranges of every parsed Python file in the pool; ``judge`` an optional provider,
    asked once about the candidates that have a source and are not containers.
    Returns packed items and every omission."""
    packer = _Packer(budget, source, declarations)
    omissions: list[Omission] = []
    scored = []

    def container(c: Candidate) -> bool:
        category = c.entity.category
        return category not in ("symbol", "file") or (
            category == "file" and c.entity.key not in declarations
        )

    asked = [c for c in pool if not container(c) and c.entity.source is not None]
    values = judged(judge, asked) if judge is not None and asked else {}
    for position, candidate in enumerate(pool):
        key = candidate.entity.key
        score, basis = values.get(key) or value(candidate)
        if container(candidate):
            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "container"))
        elif candidate.entity.source is None:
            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "no source"))
        elif score < INCLUDE_FLOOR:
            why = f"value {score:.2f} below floor" + (f", {basis}" if key in values else "")
            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", why))
        elif not packer.view(candidate.entity, False, ""):
            omissions.append(Omission(key, "selection", "no module-level source"))
        else:
            basis += ", hinted path" if candidate.hinted else ""
            scored.append(
                (not candidate.hinted, -score, position, candidate, f"value {score:.2f}, {basis}")
            )
    pieces: list[_Piece] = []
    items: list[ContextItem] = []
    planned = 0
    for *_, candidate, reason in sorted(scored, key=lambda s: s[:3]):
        entity = candidate.entity
        if planned >= MAX_ITEMS:
            omissions.append(Omission(entity.key, "selection", f"item cap {MAX_ITEMS}"))
            continue
        shown = {p.entity.key for p in pieces}
        prerequisites: list[_Piece] = []
        for outer in ancestors(entity.key):
            if outer not in shown and outer in scopes:
                header = packer.view(scopes[outer], True, f"header of {display(entity.key)}")
                prerequisites += header or packer.view(scopes[outer], False, "prerequisite")
        outline = candidate.hinted and entity.category == "file"
        for reduced in (True,) if outline and packer.view(entity, True, "") else (False, True):
            view = packer.view(entity, reduced, reason + (", header view" if reduced else ""))
            fitted = packer.fits([*pieces, *prerequisites, *view]) if view else None
            if fitted is not None:
                pieces += [*prerequisites, *view]
                items = fitted
                planned += 1
                break
        else:
            smallest = packer.view(entity, True, "") or packer.view(entity, False, "")
            assert smallest
            alone = packer.render([*prerequisites, *smallest])
            too_large = alone is None or sum(i.units for i in alone) > budget
            omissions.append(
                Omission(entity.key, "packing", "too large" if too_large else "budget")
            )
    return items, omissions

def normalized(text: str) -> str:
    """Gold content compared without indentation or blank lines (ContextBench dedents).
    Only builds the v1 ``sha256`` of tasks.json; the audit compares ``code_lines``."""
    return "\n".join(line.strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip())


def code_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Stripped non-blank lines, split on ``\\n`` only, as OXIDE numbers lines
    (``str.splitlines`` also splits on form feeds and Unicode separators)."""
    return [line.strip() for line in text.split("\n") if line.strip()]


"""Deterministic selection and packing (SPEC § Selection, § Context packing).

Routed candidates get a heuristic relevance value (the Rust ``heuristic-evidence/1``
rules), then one greedy pass takes the best candidate whose group (the item plus a
header of every enclosing declaration not yet shown) fits the remaining budget,
whole or reduced to its header view, otherwise omits it with a reason. Fit is
checked by rendering the exact payload, so ``used <= budget`` holds by construction.

A symbol's view is its declaration. A parsed Python file's view is its module-level
source (imports, constants, top-level statements): the runs of non-blank lines
between its top-level declarations, never the whole file; its header view is the
first run, and it competes only when retrieval found the file. Other files, modules
and the repository are containers without a view.

A ``paths`` hint names where the relevant code lives: candidates in a hinted file are
taken before all others (value, floor and order unchanged within each tier), and the
hinted file itself contributes only its header view, so its declarations, not its
module-level glue, get the budget.

Units are ``oxide-units-v1``: each run of word characters costs ceil(len/4), each
newline 1, other whitespace 0, any other character 1. They claim no model's
tokenizer. Payload ``oxide-payload-v3``: per item ``### <path>:<l1>-<l2> <names>``
then its source (a module-level run is named ``(module-level)``); files in
first-selection order, spans in byte order, overlapping spans of one file merged and
counted once.

An optional ``DecisionProvider`` (SPEC § DecisionProvider) may replace ``value`` for
the candidates it judges; floor, caps, tiers, order and budget stay deterministic. A
missing, abstained, invalid or failed judgment keeps the heuristic value, with the
reason. Without a provider the bundle is byte-identical to the heuristic path.
"""

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Piece:
    entity: Entity
    start: int
    end: int
    reason: str


class _Packer:
    def __init__(
        self,
        budget: int,
        source: Callable[[SourceRef], bytes],
        declarations: Mapping[str, list[tuple[int, int]]],
    ) -> None:
        self.budget = budget
        self.source = source
        self.declarations = declarations
        self.cache: dict[str, bytes] = {}

    def data(self, ref: SourceRef) -> bytes:
        if ref.path not in self.cache:
            self.cache[ref.path] = self.source(ref)
        return self.cache[ref.path]

    def render(self, pieces: list[_Piece]) -> list[ContextItem] | None:
        """Items for ``pieces``; None when a span is not UTF-8 text."""
        by_file: dict[str, list[_Piece]] = {}
        for piece in pieces:
            assert piece.entity.source is not None
            by_file.setdefault(piece.entity.source.path, []).append(piece)
        items = []
        for path, group in by_file.items():
            spans: list[list[_Piece]] = []
            for piece in sorted(group, key=lambda p: (p.start, p.end)):
                if spans and piece.start < max(p.end for p in spans[-1]):
                    spans[-1].append(piece)
                else:
                    spans.append([piece])
            for span in spans:
                item = self.item(path, span)
                if item is None:
                    return None
                items.append(item)
        return items

    def item(self, path: str, span: list[_Piece]) -> ContextItem | None:
        start, end = min(p.start for p in span), max(p.end for p in span)
        ref = span[0].entity.source
        assert ref is not None
        data = self.data(ref)
        try:
            body = data[start:end].decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return None
        entities: dict[str, ItemEntity] = {}
        for piece in span:
            source = piece.entity.source
            assert source is not None
            complete = start <= source.start and source.end <= end
            entities.setdefault(
                piece.entity.key,
                ItemEntity(piece.entity.key, display(piece.entity.key), complete, piece.reason),
            )
        labels = ", ".join(
            "(module-level)"
            if e.key.startswith("file:")
            else e.name + ("" if e.complete else " (header)")
            for e in entities.values()
        )
        first = data.count(b"\n", 0, start) + 1
        last = data.count(b"\n", 0, max(start, end - 1)) + 1
        text = f"### {path}:{first}-{last} {labels}\n{body}"
        text += "" if text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
        source = SourceRef(path, start, end, ref.digest)
        return ContextItem(source, (first, last), tuple(entities.values()), units(text), text)

    def fits(self, pieces: list[_Piece]) -> list[ContextItem] | None:
        items = self.render(pieces)
        if items is None or sum(i.units for i in items) > self.budget:
            return None
        return items

    def view(self, entity: Entity, header: bool, reason: str) -> list[_Piece]:
        """The pieces of a full or header view; empty when there is no such view."""
        source = entity.source
        assert source is not None
        if entity.category == "file":
            regions = module_regions(self.data(source), self.declarations[entity.key])
            chosen = (regions[:1] if len(regions) > 1 else []) if header else regions
            return [_Piece(entity, start, end, reason) for start, end in chosen]
        if not header:
            return [_Piece(entity, source.start, source.end, reason)]
        end = header_end(self.data(source), source.start, source.end, entity.name)
        return [] if end is None else [_Piece(entity, source.start, end, reason)]

- Identical snapshot, candidates, decision outputs, and policy inputs produce the same plan in stable order.

Structural expansion follows selected seeds through allowed relations under independent bounds, then competes for the same context budget. It does not reinterpret the selected primary list as unrestricted retrieval. Initial expansion uses deterministic role/provenance rules; novel expanded entities use heuristic evidence by default. Rejudging expanded nodes MAY be evaluated as an explicitly bounded extra pass, never an implicit iterative agent loop.

New expansion evidence cannot silently replace a selected primary. Any replacement requires a declared deterministic policy and recorded reason. Expansion-only evidence retains its origin and seed relation. Cycles, ambiguous targets, and fanout truncation are explicit.

## Context packing

`ContextPacker` is core logic that constructs the final bounded ContextBundle from the selection plan and expanded source evidence. It neither runs a judge nor initiates open-ended structural exploration; when a view does not fit, deterministic packing policy reduces or omits it with reasons.

`ContextItem` is a source-backed view of an entity or a justified coherent evidence group, with range, role, reasons, snapshot/source digest, and token cost. It may be a signature, bounded body, or scope view. View reduction follows a declared deterministic rule, preserves provenance, and signals incomplete source. It must not cut arbitrary bytes or imply a truncated body is complete.

`ContextBundle` includes ordered items, repository/snapshot/derivation, policy/model manifest, budget/counting method, source coverage and channel status, selected/expanded/packed counts, omissions, and degradation reasons. A debug trace may provide more detail than the normal user bundle without duplicating source by default.

Distinguish the canonical agent-facing context payload from the structured diagnostic envelope. Snapshot manifests, counts, and omission records may live outside the payload budget; any diagnostics rendered into agent context must be counted. An empty payload has zero tokens and no mandatory heading, so even a zero-budget request can return a typed envelope with valid empty context.

Packing MUST:

- Deduplicate overlapping source, counting merged evidence once while preserving distinct entity/reason references.
- Account for the complete canonical agent-facing context payload, including item labels, paths, separators, and in-budget summaries. Transport envelopes/UI chrome are outside the declared payload; Integrations must not add unaccounted source or explanatory context to it.
- Respect coherence groups: pack a group, use a declared smaller valid view, or omit it with a reason. Do not include an item while silently dropping its hard prerequisites.
- Produce `used_tokens <= budget_tokens` under the declared tokenizer/counting contract, including zero and very small budgets. Token usage is not a target to fill; unused budget is acceptable.
- Use stable ordering/grouping and tie-breaking. Document prioritization, rather than claiming arbitrary ordering improves agents.

The bootstrap packer needs a pinned local tokenizer/counting implementation for its canonical payload. If an estimated mode is offered, label it as estimated and never claim a strict bound for an unknown downstream tokenizer. Character/token ratios from the legacy implementation are historical controls, not hard guarantees. Choice of tokenizer and export format remains open and must be resolved before claiming packing acceptance.

## Training-data implications

The current bottleneck for learned selection is domain-specific data. Design the boundary so runtime records can become DecisionBench examples:

`query + candidate or structural region + canonical capsule + label(s) + annotation provenance`

"""Reproducible OXIDE v2 latency and memory benchmark (Python engine, ADR-0011).

    uv run python scripts/bench.py CORPUS [--iterations 5] [--warm 20] [--budget 1024]
                                          [--query TEXT ...]

Every iteration is a fresh interpreter with a fresh private data location (a new
temporary directory; real user data is never read or written), so each one starts
cold. Within an iteration:

- ``import``: ``import oxide`` in the fresh interpreter.
- ``index_cold``: ``open_repository`` + ``index()`` into the empty store (capture,
  derive, publish, FTS build).
- ``index_unchanged``: a second ``index()`` (capture + freshness check, no publish).
- ``reopen``: close, ``open_repository`` and the first read (view + FTS load).
- ``search_cold``/``context_cold``: the first call per query after reopen.
- ``search_warm``/``context_warm``: the median of ``--warm`` repeats of that call.
- ``peak_rss_mib``: the interpreter's ``ru_maxrss`` at the end.

The report (JSON on stdout) records the corpus identity (path, snapshot id, files,
bytes), the environment (Python, platform, CPUs available, package versions, OXIDE
commit, FTS availability) and min/median/max over iterations. Run it under the
same limits as recorded numbers, e.g. ``systemd-run --user --scope -p
CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G``; the limits are not detectable from inside.

55	def _link(retained: Path, blob: Path, data: bytes) -> bool:
56	    """Hard-links the current generation's blob of ``data`` into staging, if it holds
57	    exactly these bytes. A damaged blob is never carried over; a missing one, or a file
58	    system without hard links, falls back to writing."""
59	    try:
60	        os.link(retained, blob)
61	    except OSError:
62	        return False
63	    try:
64	        if blob.read_bytes() == data:
65	            return True
66	    except OSError:
67	        pass
68	    blob.unlink()  # unlink, never overwrite: the inode is shared
69	    return False

144	    def _restore(self, name: str) -> None:
145	        """Undoes publish's first rename when its second one never happened."""
146	        target, replaced = self.generations / name, self.generations / f"{name}.replaced"

151	    def _recover(self) -> str | None:
152	        pointer = self.dir / "CURRENT"
153	        if not pointer.exists():
154	            current = None

158	            except (OSError, ValueError) as error:

160	            if not _HEX64.fullmatch(current):

301	        self, staging: Path, derived: Derived, lexical: bool, snapshot: Snapshot

304	        for e in derived.entities:

311	        for site, edge in enumerate(derived.edges):
312	            ev = edge.evidence or SourceRef("", -1, -1, "")
313	            tail = (edge.name or "", site, ev.path, ev.start, ev.end)
314	            if edge.resolution == "unresolved":

318	            for target in edge.targets:
319	                rels.append((edge.source, target, edge.kind, edge.resolution, edge.basis, *tail))
320	        tables = {
321	            "Entity": entities,
322	            "Unresolved": [*unresolved.values()],
323	            "Rel": rels,
324	            "Opaque": opaque,
325	        }
326	        written = {
327	            table: _write_csv(staging / f"{table}.csv", rows) for table, rows in tables.items()
328	        }
329	        size = sum((staging / f"{table}.csv").stat().st_size for table in tables)
330	        pool = load_pool(size)

332	        # keep one. FTS indexing does not: on 2 threads its BM25 scores drift by one ULP in

334	        # writes pages: an auto-checkpoint inside CREATE_FTS_INDEX would leave its temporary
335	        # tables as dead pages in the file (docs/fts-footprint.md).

content.text:
I made one change that held up in benchmarks and committed it. No context-quality change passed, so packing and selection are unchanged.

**Committed**
- `c35d67c` speeds up the Python resolver (`src/oxide/core/languages/python_resolve.py`). It used to scan every child declaration and every import of a scope on each name lookup (about 1M iterations on xarray). It now builds a name-to-declarations map and a star-import flag once per scope. The output is unchanged: same entity and relation counts, and the ContextBench gate inside `mise run verify` passes (439 passed, 7 skipped).
- Results on xarray, limited to 200% CPU and 3 GB:

  | Measurement | Before | After | Change |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Full index from scratch (`scripts/bench.py`, median of 5) | 1.476 s | 1.383 s | −6% |
  | Re-index after editing one file | 0.933 s | 0.823 s | −12% |
  | Resolution step within that re-index | 0.33 s | 0.22 s | −33% |

  The verdict is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.
- `8455135` commits the two REJECT verdicts (`cover-selector`, `excerpt`) that an earlier session had left uncommitted in `docs/decisions.md`.

**Tried and reverted**
- **Shorter item headings:** I dropped the labels of entities already visible inside their parent's code. It saved about 1% of units, but recall didn't change at any budget, so it wasn't worth a payload format change.
- **Faster CSV writing:** switching to the standard-library `csv` writer for the database load made publishing no faster (0.57 s vs 0.60 s, within noise).

**What limits further gains**
- **Context quality:** at a 1024-unit budget, the main loss is ranking. Unrelated items use up the budget before the right code (`psf__requests-2931`). The item cap isn't the problem: raising it changed no recall. Earlier verdicts already rejected the obvious fixes (cover selector, excerpts, PPR, order tiebreak, lexical body fields).
- **Re-index speed:** publishing (about 0.57 s) now dominates, because each re-index rebuilds the whole database and search index. Making that incremental would mean changing how index versions are stored and published. Re-resolving only changed files was already judged not worth it.

I didn't run the TypeScript gate (`mise run contextbench-ts`) or the 3.12/3.14 Python runs (`mise run pythons`). The change only touches the Python resolver and its output is identical, so the risk there is low. The speed numbers come from one corpus (xarray) and are not pushed.

Stop hook feedback:
[Improve OXIDE's context intelligence, token efficiency, and incremental indexing speed through better algorithms. This is is additional to the first one]: The condition has three parts and only one is met. Incremental indexing speed improved: commit c35d67c cut one-file re-index from 0.933 s to 0.823 s (−12%). Context intelligence and token efficiency did not improve. The transcript says "No context-quality change passed, so packing and selection are unchanged," and the label-elision experiment that saved about 1% of units was reverted because recall did not change. No improvement to context intelligence or token efficiency has been committed.

A ``paths`` hint names where the relevant code lives: candidates in a hinted file are
taken before all others (value, floor and order unchanged within each tier), and the
hinted file itself contributes only its header view, so its declarations, not its
module-level glue, get the budget.

Units are ``oxide-units-v1``: each run of word characters costs ceil(len/4), each
newline 1, other whitespace 0, any other character 1. They claim no model's
tokenizer. Payload ``oxide-payload-v3``: per item ``### <path>:<l1>-<l2> <names>``
then its source (a module-level run is named ``(module-level)``); files in
first-selection order, spans in byte order, overlapping spans of one file merged and
counted once.

An optional ``DecisionProvider`` (SPEC § DecisionProvider) may replace ``value`` for
the candidates it judges; floor, caps, tiers, order and budget stay deterministic. A
missing, abstained, invalid or failed judgment keeps the heuristic value, with the
reason. Without a provider the bundle is byte-identical to the heuristic path.

content.text:
I committed two improvements, one for indexing speed and one for context quality and token efficiency. Both passed `mise run verify` (440 passed, 7 skipped) and nothing is pushed.

**1. Faster re-indexing (`c35d67c`).** On each name lookup, the Python resolver used to scan every declaration and import in a scope. It now builds a name lookup once per scope, which makes indexing faster with output unchanged. On xarray:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Re-index after editing one file | 0.933 s | 0.823 s (−12%) |
| Full index from scratch | 1.476 s | 1.383 s (−6%) |

**2. Fewer headings in context output (`2be287a`).** When two pieces of code from the same file had only blank lines between them, each got its own `### path:lines` heading. Those repeated headings used about 4% of the budget. They now share one item and one heading, so the saved budget buys more source code. Which code gets selected is unchanged.

| ContextBench | Before | After |
|---|---|---|

def _link(retained: Path, blob: Path, data: bytes) -> bool:
    """Hard-links the current generation's blob of ``data`` into staging, if it holds
    exactly these bytes. A damaged blob is never carried over; a missing one, or a file
    system without hard links, falls back to writing."""
    try:
        os.link(retained, blob)
    except OSError:
        return False
    try:
        if blob.read_bytes() == data:
            return True
    except OSError:
        pass
    blob.unlink()  # unlink, never overwrite: the inode is shared
    return False

    def _restore(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Undoes publish's first rename when its second one never happened."""
        target, replaced = self.generations / name, self.generations / f"{name}.replaced"
        if not target.exists() and replaced.is_dir():
            os.rename(replaced, target)
            _fsync(self.generations)

    def _recover(self) -> str | None:
        pointer = self.dir / "CURRENT"
        if not pointer.exists():
            current = None
        else:
            try:
                current = pointer.read_text(encoding="ascii").strip()
            except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"{pointer}: unreadable ({error}); remove {self.dir}") from error
            if not _HEX64.fullmatch(current):
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"{pointer}: not a generation name; remove {self.dir}")
            # A crash between publish's two renames: the replaced generation goes back
            # in place. It was unreadable or stale, so the next index() rebuilds it.
            self._restore(current)
            if not (self.generations / current / "MANIFEST.json").is_file():
                # Ambiguous: nothing is deleted, nothing is served.
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"{pointer} names a missing generation; remove {self.dir}")
        # No view can be pinned before this owner existed: everything else is garbage.
        for entry in self.generations.iterdir():
            if entry.name != current:
                shutil.rmtree(entry, ignore_errors=True)
        return current

    def view(self) -> View:
        if self.current is None:
            raise NotIndexed(f"{self.root} has not been indexed")
        if self._view is None:
            self._view = View(self.generations / self.current, self.repo_id)
        return self._view

    def _drop_view(self) -> None:
        if self._view is not None:
            self._view.close()
            self._view = None

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._drop_view()
        self._release()

    def _name(self, snapshot_id: str, components: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
        derivation = derivation_id(components)
        identity = json.dumps([self.repo_id, snapshot_id, derivation]).encode()
        return hashlib.sha256(identity).hexdigest(), derivation

    def is_current(self, snapshot_id: str, components: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
        """Whether this capture and derivation are already published, readable and backed
        by every retained source file."""
        if self._name(snapshot_id, components)[0] != self.current:
            return False
        try:
            self.view().verify_sources()
            return True
        except (IncompatibleIndex, StoreCorrupt):
            self._drop_view()
            return False  # unreadable under this OXIDE: rebuilt, never migrated

    def previous(self) -> View | None:
        """The current generation if it is readable under this OXIDE, else None."""
        try:
            return self.view()
        except (NotIndexed, IncompatibleIndex, StoreCorrupt):
            self._drop_view()
            return None

    def publish(
        self,
        capture: Capture,
        derived: Derived,
        components: dict[str, str],
        lexical_unavailable: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Builds, seals and atomically publishes the generation."""
        name, derivation = self._name(capture.snapshot_id, components)
        staging = self.generations / f"{name}.staging"
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
        staging.mkdir()
        try:
            # LadybugDB releases the GIL and builds the FTS index on one thread, so the
            # source blobs are written meanwhile (docs/fts-footprint.md § 4).
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(1) as pool:
                retaining = pool.submit(self._retain, staging, capture)
                snapshot = Snapshot(self.repo_id, capture.snapshot_id, derivation)
                rows = self._load(staging, derived, lexical_unavailable is None, snapshot)
                retaining.result()
            facts = json.dumps(derived.facts, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
            (staging / "facts.json").write_bytes(facts)
            manifest = {
                "schema": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                "repo_id": self.repo_id,
                "snapshot_id": capture.snapshot_id,
                "derivation_id": derivation,
                "components": components,
                "lexical_unavailable": lexical_unavailable,
                "files": [
                    [f.path, f.digest, f.size, f.language, f.coverage, list(f.diagnostics)]
                    for f in derived.files
                ],
                "skipped": [[s.path, s.reason] for s in capture.skipped],
                "case_collisions": [list(group) for group in capture.case_collisions],
                "entities": len(derived.entities),
                "relations": len(derived.edges),
                "rows": rows,
                "facts": {"format": FACTS_FORMAT, "digest": digest(facts)},

                # renames is undone on the next open (_recover); a failure, just below.
                # Close our own view of it first: Windows can't rename a directory with
                # open files.

            shutil.rmtree(self.generations / str(stale), ignore_errors=True)

    def _retain(self, staging: Path, capture: Capture) -> None:
        """Makes the captured bytes durable in the staging's ``source`` directory."""
        source = staging / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        retained = self.generations / self.current / "source" if self.current else None

            blob = source / name

                continue  # a linked blob was made durable when its generation was sealed
            blob.write_bytes(f.data)
            _fsync(blob)
        _fsync(source)

    def _seal(self, staging: Path, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Writes the manifest, then makes the staging durable."""
        (staging / "MANIFEST.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        for path in staging.iterdir():
            if path.is_file():
                _fsync(path)
        _fsync(staging)

    def _load(
        self, staging: Path, derived: Derived, lexical: bool, snapshot: Snapshot
    ) -> dict[str, int]:
        entities: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
        for e in derived.entities:
            src = e.source or SourceRef("", -1, -1, "")
            row = (e.key, e.category, e.kind, e.name, e.signature or "", src.path, src.start)
            entities.append((*row, src.end, src.digest, e.test, document(e)))
        rels: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
        opaque: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
        unresolved: dict[str, tuple[object, ...]] = {}
        for site, edge in enumerate(derived.edges):
            ev = edge.evidence or SourceRef("", -1, -1, "")
            tail = (edge.name or "", site, ev.path, ev.start, ev.end)
            if edge.resolution == "unresolved":
                node = unresolved_key(edge.name or "")
                unresolved.setdefault(node, (node, node[2:]))
                opaque.append((edge.source, node, edge.kind, edge.basis, *tail))
            for target in edge.targets:
                rels.append((edge.source, target, edge.kind, edge.resolution, edge.basis, *tail))
        tables = {
            "Entity": entities,
            "Unresolved": [*unresolved.values()],
            "Rel": rels,
            "Opaque": opaque,
        }
        written = {
            table: _write_csv(staging / f"{table}.csv", rows) for table, rows in tables.items()
        }
        size = sum((staging / f"{table}.csv").stat().st_size for table in tables)
        pool = load_pool(size)
        # The staging load alone gets a second thread for COPY (rows unchanged); read views
        # keep one. FTS indexing does not: on 2 threads its BM25 scores drift by one ULP in
        # ~10% of builds (indexing-throughput § 9 at 013e791). Only the final CHECKPOINT
        # writes pages: an auto-checkpoint inside CREATE_FTS_INDEX would leave its temporary
        # tables as dead pages in the file (docs/fts-footprint.md).
        db = ladybug.Database(
            str(staging / "graph.lbug"),
            buffer_pool_size=pool,
            max_num_threads=2,
            auto_checkpoint=False,
        )
        conn = ladybug.Connection(db)
        try:
            if db.get_storage_version() != STORAGE_FORMAT:
                raise IncompatibleIndex(f"ladybug storage format is not {STORAGE_FORMAT}")
            for statement in _SCHEMA:
                _rows(conn, statement)
            _rows(conn, "BEGIN TRANSACTION")
            for table in tables:
                csv = staging / f"{table}.csv"
                if written[table]:
                    options = "header=false, quote='\"', escape='\"', delim=',', parallel=false"
                    _rows(conn, f"COPY {table} FROM {_literal(csv)} ({options})")
                csv.unlink()
            _rows(conn, "CREATE (:Identity {key: $key})", {"key": identity(snapshot)})
            _rows(conn, "COMMIT")
            counted = {
                "Entity": "MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN count(e)",
                "Unresolved": "MATCH (u:Unresolved) RETURN count(u)",
                "Rel": "MATCH ()-[r:Rel]->() RETURN count(r)",
                "Opaque": "MATCH ()-[r:Opaque]->() RETURN count(r)",
            }
            read = {table: _rows(conn, query)[0][0] for table, query in counted.items()}
            if read != written:
                # COPY can drop rows whose endpoints are missing; never publish that.
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"read back {read}, wrote {written}")
            if lexical:
                conn.set_max_threads_for_exec(1)
                _rows(conn, f"LOAD EXTENSION {_literal(fts_location())}")
                _rows(
                    conn,
                    "CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('Entity', 'lexical', ['terms'], stemmer := 'porter')",
                )
            _rows(conn, "CHECKPOINT")
        finally:
            conn.close()
            db.close()

"""Derivation: captured source to entities and typed relations (SPEC § Indexing and publication).

Every file is file evidence with explicit coverage, whether or not a language slice
understands it. The derivation identity names every component that shapes the
derived knowledge, so a change in any of them is a different generation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import partial
from importlib.metadata import version
from typing import Any, Literal

from oxide.capture import Capture
from oxide.core.languages import (
    c,
    c_resolve,
    cpp,
    cpp_facts,
    cpp_macros,
    cpp_resolve,
    go,
    go_resolve,
    java,
    java_facts,
    java_resolve,
    python,
    python_resolve,
    rust,
    rust_resolve,
    typescript,
    typescript_resolve,
    typescript_syntax,
)
from oxide.core.languages.python_resolve import Edge
from oxide.core.retrieval import TERMS_VERSION
from oxide.models import Coverage, Entity, FileInfo, OxideError, SourceRef

ID_NAMESPACE = "oxide-id-v2"
TREE_PROJECTION = "1"
# ``facts.json``: one section of encoded facts by digest per dialect (the same bytes
# parse differently across grammars); include each slice's facts version.
FACTS_FORMAT = (
    f"oxide-facts-v2 {python.FACTS_VERSION} {typescript.FACTS_VERSION} "
    f"{typescript.JAVASCRIPT_FACTS_VERSION} {go.FACTS_VERSION} {rust.FACTS_VERSION} "
    f"{java.FACTS_VERSION} {c.FACTS_VERSION} {cpp.FACTS_VERSION}"
)

Dialect = Literal["python", "typescript", "tsx", "javascript", "go", "rust", "java", "c", "cpp"]
CPP_SUFFIXES = (
    ".cc",
    ".cpp",
    ".cxx",
    ".c++",
    ".hh",
    ".hpp",
    ".hxx",
    ".h++",
    ".ipp",
    ".tpp",
    ".inl",
)


def dialect(path: str) -> Dialect | None:
    """The language slice and grammar that parse ``path``, None when none does."""
    if path.endswith(".go"):
        return "go"
    if path.endswith(".rs"):
        return "rust"
    if path.endswith(".java"):
        return "java"
    if path.endswith((".c", ".h")):
        return "c"
    if path.endswith(CPP_SUFFIXES):
        return "cpp"
    return "python" if path.endswith(".py") else typescript_syntax.dialect(path)


def source_dialect(path: str, data: bytes) -> Dialect | None:
    """``dialect``, except that a ``.h`` file with C++ syntax is C++ (docs/cpp.md)."""
    found = dialect(path)
    return (
        "cpp" if found == "c" and path.endswith(".h") and cpp_macros.is_cplusplus(data) else found
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Derived:
    files: tuple[FileInfo, ...]
    entities: tuple[Entity, ...]
    edges: tuple[Edge, ...]
    # Encoded facts of every parsed file, by dialect and digest (``FACTS_FORMAT``): a
    # cache for the next derivation, not knowledge.
    facts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
    reused: int = field(default=0, compare=False)  # files whose cached facts were usable


def components(storage: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Named versions of everything that shapes a generation (ADR-0010 § DerivationId)."""
    parser = f"tree-sitter={version('tree-sitter')}"
    return {
        "id-namespace": ID_NAMESPACE,
        "python": python.VERSION,
        "python-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-python={version('tree-sitter-python')}",
        "typescript": typescript.VERSION,
        "typescript-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-typescript={version('tree-sitter-typescript')}",
        "javascript": typescript.JAVASCRIPT_VERSION,
        "javascript-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-javascript={version('tree-sitter-javascript')}",
        "go": go.VERSION,
        "go-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-go={version('tree-sitter-go')}",
        "rust": rust.VERSION,
        "rust-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-rust={version('tree-sitter-rust')}",
        "java": java.VERSION,
        "java-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-java={version('tree-sitter-java')}",
        "c": c.VERSION,
        "c-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-c={version('tree-sitter-c')}",
        "cpp": cpp.VERSION,
        "cpp-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-cpp={version('tree-sitter-cpp')}",
        "terms": TERMS_VERSION,
        "tree-projection": TREE_PROJECTION,
        **storage,
    }


def derivation_id(parts: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    encoded = json.dumps(sorted(parts.items()), separators=(",", ":")).encode()
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()


def validate(derived: Derived) -> None:
    """Publication invariants: unique keys, existing endpoints, and exactly one physical
    parent for every entity but the repository (so TreeIndex cannot contradict identity)."""
    keys: set[str] = set()
    for entity in derived.entities:
        if entity.key in keys:
            raise OxideError(f"invalid derivation: duplicate entity {entity.key}")
        keys.add(entity.key)
    parents: dict[str, int] = {}
    for edge in derived.edges:
        missing = [k for k in (edge.source, *edge.targets) if k not in keys]
        if missing:
            raise OxideError(f"invalid derivation: {edge.kind} edge to unknown {missing[0]}")
        if edge.kind == "contains":
            parents[edge.targets[0]] = parents.get(edge.targets[0], 0) + 1
    for key in keys - {"repo"}:
        if parents.get(key) != 1:
            raise OxideError(f"invalid derivation: {key} has {parents.get(key, 0)} parents")


def _reuse[P](
    raw: Any, data: bytes, decode: Callable[[Any, int], P], parse: Callable[[bytes], P | str]
) -> tuple[P | str, bool]:
    """Cached facts when ``decode`` accepts them, else a parse; and whether reused."""
    if raw is not None:
        try:
            return decode(raw, len(data)), True
        except ValueError:
            pass  # unusable: parsed and replaced, so it never spreads
    return parse(data), False


def derive(capture: Capture, repo_id: str, cached: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Derived:
    """``cached`` holds facts of an earlier derivation under the same components, by
    dialect and file digest. Parsing is a pure function of the bytes, so reusing them
    derives exactly what parsing would; an entry ``decode`` rejects is parsed instead.
    Resolution always runs over the whole capture."""
    cached = cached or {}
    facts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    reused = 0
    files: list[FileInfo] = []
    entities = [Entity("repo", "repository", "repository", repo_id, None, None, False)]
    edges: list[Edge] = []
    py_sources: list[tuple[str, str, python.Parsed]] = []
    ts_sources: list[tuple[str, str, typescript_syntax.Parsed]] = []
    go_sources: list[tuple[str, str, go.Parsed]] = []
    rs_sources: list[tuple[str, str, rust.Parsed]] = []
    java_sources: list[tuple[str, str, java.Parsed]] = []
    c_sources: list[tuple[str, str, c.Parsed]] = []
    cpp_sources: list[tuple[str, str, cpp.Parsed]] = []
    for f in capture.files:
        key = f"file:{f.path}"
        name = f.path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        source = SourceRef(f.path, 0, len(f.data), f.digest)
        entities.append(Entity(key, "file", "file", name, None, source, False))
        edges.append(Edge("contains", "repo", (key,), "resolved", "syntactic", None, None))
        lang = source_dialect(f.path, f.data)
        if lang is None:
            files.append(FileInfo(f.path, f.digest, len(f.data), "unknown", "unsupported", ()))
            continue
        section = cached.get(lang)
        raw = section.get(f.digest) if isinstance(section, dict) else None
        language = lang if lang not in ("typescript", "tsx") else "typescript"
        diagnostics: list[str] | str
        if lang == "python":
            py, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, python.decode, python.parse)
            if not isinstance(py, str):
                py_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, py))
                encoded = raw if hit else python.encode(py)
            diagnostics = py if isinstance(py, str) else py.diagnostics
        elif lang == "go":
            gp, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, go.decode, go.parse)
            if not isinstance(gp, str):
                go_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, gp))
                encoded = raw if hit else go.encode(gp)
            diagnostics = gp if isinstance(gp, str) else gp.diagnostics
        elif lang == "rust":
            rp, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, rust.decode, rust.parse)
            if not isinstance(rp, str):
                rs_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, rp))
                encoded = raw if hit else rust.encode(rp)
            diagnostics = rp if isinstance(rp, str) else rp.diagnostics
        elif lang == "java":
            jp, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, java_facts.decode, java.parse)
            if not isinstance(jp, str):
                java_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, jp))
                encoded = raw if hit else java_facts.encode(jp)
            diagnostics = jp if isinstance(jp, str) else jp.diagnostics
        elif lang == "c":
            cp, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, c.decode, c.parse)
            if not isinstance(cp, str):
                c_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, cp))
                encoded = raw if hit else c.encode(cp)
            diagnostics = cp if isinstance(cp, str) else cp.diagnostics
        elif lang == "cpp":
            xp, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, cpp_facts.decode, cpp.parse)
            if not isinstance(xp, str):
                cpp_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, xp))
                encoded = raw if hit else cpp_facts.encode(xp)
            diagnostics = xp if isinstance(xp, str) else xp.diagnostics
        else:
            parse = partial(typescript.parse, language=lang)
            ts, hit = _reuse(raw, f.data, typescript.decode, parse)
            if not isinstance(ts, str):
                ts_sources.append((f.path, f.digest, ts))
                encoded = raw if hit else typescript.encode(ts)
            diagnostics = ts if isinstance(ts, str) else ts.diagnostics
        reused += hit
        if isinstance(diagnostics, str):
            info = FileInfo(f.path, f.digest, len(f.data), language, "unsupported", (diagnostics,))
        else:
            facts.setdefault(lang, {})[f.digest] = encoded
            coverage: Coverage = "partial" if diagnostics else "complete"
            info = FileInfo(f.path, f.digest, len(f.data), language, coverage, tuple(diagnostics))
        files.append(info)
    python_resolve.Resolver(py_sources).derive(entities, edges)
    parsed = {path for path, _, _ in ts_sources}
    others = {f.path: f.data for f in capture.files if f.path not in parsed}
    typescript_resolve.Resolver(ts_sources, others).derive(entities, edges)
    mods = {p: d for p, d in others.items() if p.rpartition("/")[2] == "go.mod"}
    go_resolve.Resolver(go_sources, mods).derive(entities, edges)
    manifests = {p: d for p, d in others.items() if p.rpartition("/")[2] == "Cargo.toml"}
    rust_resolve.Resolver(rs_sources, manifests).derive(entities, edges)
    java_resolve.Resolver(java_sources).derive(entities, edges)
    paths = {f.path for f in capture.files}
    c_resolve.Resolver(c_sources, paths).derive(entities, edges)
    cpp_resolve.Resolver(cpp_sources, c_sources, paths).derive(entities, edges)
    return Derived(tuple(files), tuple(entities), tuple(edges), facts, reused)

def index(self, *, progress: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> IndexReport:
        """Captures the worktree and publishes a new generation, or reports ``unchanged``
        when the capture and derivation equal the current one. Supported source
        files whose bytes the current generation already parsed reuse its facts;
        resolution and publication always cover the whole capture, so the result equals
        a full rebuild. ``progress`` receives a line as each stage starts."""
        started = time.perf_counter()
        report = progress or (lambda line: None)
        store = self.store
        report(f"capturing {self.root}")
        # The data location is never source, wherever it sits (compared by identity).
        snapshot = capture(self.root, exclude=(store.data, store.data / "repos"))
        lexical_unavailable = fts_unavailable(fts_location())
        parts = components(storage_components(lexical_unavailable is None))
        built = not store.is_current(snapshot.snapshot_id, parts)
        previous: Snapshot | None = None
        changes: tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...] = ((), (), ())
        parsed = reused = 0
        if built:
            old = store.previous()
            before = {f.path: f.digest for f in old.files.values()} if old else {}
            after = {f.path: f.digest for f in snapshot.files}
            changes = (
                tuple(p for p in after if p not in before),
                tuple(p for p in after if p in before and before[p] != after[p]),
                tuple(sorted(p for p in before if p not in after)),
            )
            previous = old.snapshot if old else None
            cached = old.facts() if old else {}
            sources = [
                (lang, f.digest)
                for f in snapshot.files
                if (lang := source_dialect(f.path, f.data)) is not None
            ]
            hits = sum(isinstance(s := cached.get(lang), dict) and d in s for lang, d in sources)
            report(
                f"deriving {len(after)} files: parsing {len(sources) - hits} source files, "
                f"reusing {hits}"
            )
            # A build allocates millions of objects that hold no cycles; the cyclic GC only
            # re-scans them (~8% of a build, indexing-throughput at 013e791). The switch
            # is process-global, so the caller's state is restored on every exit.
            enabled = gc.isenabled()
            gc.disable()
            try:
                derived = derive(snapshot, store.repo_id, cached)
                reused, parsed = derived.reused, len(sources) - derived.reused
                if reused < hits:
                    report(f"{hits - reused} cached parse facts were unusable and parsed again")
                validate(derived)
                report(
                    f"publishing {len(derived.entities)} entities, {len(derived.edges)} relations"
                )
                store.publish(snapshot, derived, parts, lexical_unavailable)
            finally:
                if enabled:
                    gc.enable()
        view = store.view()
        files = view.files.values()
        return IndexReport(
            snapshot=view.snapshot,
            status="built" if built else "unchanged",
            files=len(view.files),
            entities=view.counts[0],
            relations=view.counts[1],
            partial=tuple(f.path for f in files if f.coverage == "partial"),
            unsupported=sum(f.coverage == "unsupported" for f in files),
            skipped=snapshot.skipped,
            case_collisions=snapshot.case_collisions,
            lexical=view.lexical_unavailable or "available",
            seconds=time.perf_counter() - started,
            previous=previous,
            added=changes[0],
            modified=changes[1],
            deleted=changes[2],
            parsed=parsed,
            reused=reused,
        )

content.text:
I couldn't make incremental indexing substantially faster without losing exactness, so I kept no code change for that part. The full rebuild after an edit is already close to what this store allows. I recorded the result as a REJECT row in `docs/decisions.md` (`665e97f`).

**Baselines:** this was already done before your message. `2be287a` froze Python `baseline-v20` and TypeScript `baseline-v17` after the TypeScript gate passed.

**Where the time goes.** Re-indexing xarray after a one-file edit takes 0.83 s:

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Write the new generation to disk | 0.58 s |
|   of which: build the full-text search index | 0.20 s |
|   of which: load the relation tables | 0.15 s |
|   of which: write the CSV files | 0.08 s |
| Re-resolve all files | 0.22 s |
| Scan the worktree | 0.02 s |

**Updating only the changed rows, measured and rejected:**
- **Very few rows change.** The edit touches 157 entities and about 140 relations.
- **But nearly every relation row is rewritten.** Each relation is stored with its position in one repo-wide edge list, and one inserted definition shifts 28,159 of those positions.
- **Slower:** patching a copy of the previous database took 0.95 s, against 0.52 s to rebuild it from scratch.
- **Not exact:** LadybugDB's in-place search-index updates silently dropped results. One query returned 1054 hits where a fresh build returns 1065, so search results would differ from a full rebuild.
- **No fix gets under the rebuild.** Even with positions that don't shift, rebuilding the search index (0.20 s) plus the database's write-out step (0.13–0.15 s) costs about as much as the full load.

**Other options I measured but didn't build:**
- **Re-resolving only files affected by the edit** saves at most 0.17 s (about 20%). Exact dependency tracking is hard here: Python method calls are resolved against every class in the repo, so a new method anywhere can change edges in any file. I judged the risk to exact results too high for that gain.
- **Building the search index while the CSV files are written** saves at most 0.06 s, which wasn't worth the complexity.

I didn't need extra research for this, because every option was settled by direct measurement. All numbers come from one corpus (xarray) on tmpfs; on real disks, the time to flush files to disk is the same for every option.

Decision for you: if you still want the dependency-aware re-resolution for Python, say so. The cost is the exactness risk and a maximum gain of about 20% on a one-file re-index.

A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: "Make OXIDE's incremental indexing substantially faster using proven techniques from security scanners and incremental analysis systems.     def is_current(self, snapshot_id: str, components: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
        """Whether this capture and derivation are already published, readable and backed
        by every retained source file."""
        if self._name(snapshot_id, components)[0] != self.current:
            return False
        try:
            self.view().verify_sources()
            return True
        except (IncompatibleIndex, StoreCorrupt):
            self._drop_view()
            return False  # unreadable under this OXIDE: rebuilt, never migrated

    def previous(self) -> View | None:
        """The current generation if it is readable under this OXIDE, else None."""
        try:
            return self.view()
        except (NotIndexed, IncompatibleIndex, StoreCorrupt):
            self._drop_view()
            return None

    def publish(
        self,
        capture: Capture,
        derived: Derived,
        components: dict[str, str],
        lexical_unavailable: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Builds, seals and atomically publishes the generation."""
        name, derivation = self._name(capture.snapshot_id, components)
        staging = self.generations / f"{name}.staging"
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
        staging.mkdir()
        try:
            # LadybugDB releases the GIL and builds the FTS index on one thread, so the
            # source blobs are written meanwhile (docs/fts-footprint.md § 4).
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(1) as pool:
                retaining = pool.submit(self._retain, staging, capture)
                snapshot = Snapshot(self.repo_id, capture.snapshot_id, derivation)
                rows = self._load(staging, derived, lexical_unavailable is None, snapshot)
                retaining.result()
            facts = json.dumps(derived.facts, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
            (staging / "facts.json").write_bytes(facts)
            manifest = {
                "schema": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                "repo_id": self.repo_id,
                "snapshot_id": capture.snapshot_id,
                "derivation_id": derivation,
                "components": components,
                "lexical_unavailable": lexical_unavailable,
                "files": [
                    [f.path, f.digest, f.size, f.language, f.coverage, list(f.diagnostics)]
                    for f in derived.files
                ],
                "skipped": [[s.path, s.reason] for s in capture.skipped],
                "case_collisions": [list(group) for group in capture.case_collisions],
                "entities": len(derived.entities),
                "relations": len(derived.edges),
                "rows": rows,
                "facts": {"format": FACTS_FORMAT, "digest": digest(facts)},
            }
            self._seal(staging, manifest)
            target = self.generations / name
            if target.exists():
                # The unreadable generation this rebuild replaces. A crash between the two
                # renames is undone on the next open (_recover); a failure, just below.
                # Close our own view of it first: Windows can't rename a directory with
                # open files.
                self._drop_view()
                os.rename(target, self.generations / f"{name}.replaced")
            os.rename(staging, target)
            _fsync(self.generations)
        except BaseException:
            shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
            self._restore(name)
            raise
        _write_atomic(self.dir / "CURRENT", name.encode())
        previous, self.current = self.current, name
        self._drop_view()
        for stale in {previous, f"{name}.replaced"} - {name, None}:
            shutil.rmtree(self.generations / str(stale), ignore_errors=True)

    def _retain(self, staging: Path, capture: Capture) -> None:
        """Makes the captured bytes durable in the staging's ``source`` directory."""
        source = staging / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        retained = self.generations / self.current / "source" if self.current else None
        for f in capture.files:
            name = f.digest.removeprefix("sha256:")
            blob = source / name
            if blob.exists() or (retained and _link(retained / name, blob, f.data)):
                continue  # a linked blob was made durable when its generation was sealed
            blob.write_bytes(f.data)
            _fsync(blob)
        _fsync(source)

    def _seal(self, staging: Path, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Writes the manifest, then makes the staging durable."""
        (staging / "MANIFEST.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        for path in staging.iterdir():
            if path.is_file():
                _fsync(path)
        _fsync(staging)

import oxide

    with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=d + "/data") as repo:
        def run(label):
            marks = []
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            r = repo.index(progress=lambda l: marks.append((time.perf_counter() - t0, l.split()[0])))
            end = time.perf_counter() - t0
            seq = marks + [(end, "end")]
            print(label, " ".join(f"{a[1]}={b[0]-a[0]:.3f}" for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:])), f"total={end:.3f}")

            with open(f"{root}/{sys.argv[2]}", "a") as f: f.write(f"\ndef _oxide_probe_{i}():\n    return {i}\n")
            run("incr")
        run("same")

Cost: peak RSS 1340→1591 MB (VS Code) from the concurrent pools. CREATE_FTS_INDEX needs ~10 MiB of pool per MB of documents (VS Code 23.2 MB: 256 MiB fails, 270 MiB fits), so the lexical pool is `BUFFER_POOL + 10 × bytes`; at 2× all 14 VS Code corpora failed. In-place FTS patching was 5× faster than a rebuild but left one-ULP drift in multi-term BM25 sums: REJECT. |

content.text:
Re-indexing after a one-file edit is now 17–24% faster, with identical results. It's committed as `da922b9` (not pushed). That's a solid gain, but it leaves most of the re-index time where it was.

**What changed:** the search index now lives in its own database file per generation (`lexical.lbug`), and the store schema moved to v4.
- **Built in parallel:** it's built alongside the main graph instead of after it.
- **Reused when unchanged:** each edit changes the bytes of many entities, but rarely their searchable text (name, signature, file path). When that text hasn't changed, the new generation reuses the previous index through a hard link and doesn't rebuild it.

**Speed:**

| Re-index after | ansible | xarray |
|---|---|---|
| Adding a definition | 2.53 → 2.02 s (−20%) | 0.81 → 0.67 s (−17%) |
| A body-only edit | 2.52 → 1.91 s (−24%) | 0.81 → 0.66 s (−19%) |
| Cold index, 82 TS corpora | 418 → 352 s (−16%) | |

**Exactness:** both ContextBench suites give results identical to the previous baselines once the derivation id is replaced, and their metrics files are byte-identical. The derivation id changes because it includes the store schema version. I froze these runs as Python `baseline-v21` and TS `baseline-v18`. `mise run verify` passes (446 passed, 7 skipped), and so does the TS gate (17 passed).

**One bug caught on the way:** the first TS run failed to index all 14 VS Code corpora because the search index ran out of memory. It needs about 10 MiB of memory per MB of indexed text, five times what the graph load gets. With that sizing, nothing fails.

**Cost:** peak memory on VS Code rose from 1340 to 1591 MB (+19%), because both builds now run at once.

**Rejected:** patching the search index in place was 5× faster than a rebuild. But it changed the last bit of some multi-term search scores compared with a fresh build, so it wasn't exact.

**Not covered:**
- I only timed on Linux tmpfs. On a filesystem without hard links, the index is simply rebuilt.
- The rest of the re-index time is untouched: re-resolving all files (0.64 s on ansible) and loading the graph tables.
- The new memory sizing comes from one repository (VS Code).

Make OXIDE's new split graph/FTS indexing architecture production-ready. Optimize memory usage, verify exact correctness and crash recovery across platforms, and improve performance wherever measurements justify it. After that, commit to main

def test_unchanged_sources_are_linked_never_rewritten(repo_copy: Path, private_data: Path) -> None:
    oxide.index_repository(repo_copy)
    before = {b.name: b.stat().st_ino for b in blobs(private_data)}
    edited = next(p for p in sorted(repo_copy.rglob("*.py")) if p.stat().st_size)
    old = edited.read_bytes()
    edited.write_bytes(old + b"\n# edited\n")
    assert oxide.index_repository(repo_copy).status == "built"
    after = {b.name: b.stat().st_ino for b in blobs(private_data)}
    gone = digest(old).removeprefix("sha256:")
    assert set(after) - set(before) == {digest(edited.read_bytes()).removeprefix("sha256:")}
    assert all(after[n] == ino for n, ino in before.items() if n != gone)

) -> None:
    seen: list[bool] = []
